80252.subject: 😬 Sam Altman wants you to accept some bad things
80252.body:
----------
######           [Subscribe](https://academynews.genai.works/)   -    [Collaborate with us](https://utm.genai.works/r/cq9vsh4)


--------------------
View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/8776fa6e-e2d0-4aec-9648-1bed6de3a659/GenAI_Daily_Banner.jpg?t=1778687445)
Caption: 


----------

----------
**Welcome back!** Sam Altman says the world should accept some bad things in exchange for AI, the same weekend the man in charge of OpenAI's safety reports explained why he quit. At work, your coworkers are starting to talk like Claude. Trump finally named his AI czar to run a new Super Intelligence Force. And OpenAI is promising Codex users an upgrade or a usage reset every day for 28 days.

**In today's Generative AI Newsletter:**

* **OpenAI:** Which bad things does Sam Altman want you to live with?

* **Claude:** Why are your coworkers suddenly calling everyone brilliant?

* **White House:** Who's running Trump's new Super Intelligence Force?

* **Codex:** What does OpenAI owe you every day for the next 28 days?


----------







----------
## Altman wants the world to accept some bad things

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/8ab38bdf-9ded-4325-8792-33ddaf2091e5/Accept_Some_Bad_Things.png?t=1791190605)
Caption: 

Sam Altman [told POLITICO](https://www.politico.com/news/2026/10/04/sam-altman-decoded-interview-ai-01106217) that **the world should accept some bad things happening** for the benefits of AI. He said it when asked where OpenAI and Anthropic disagree.

* The bad things he named include major hacks and scams.

* He thinks people will do orders of magnitude more good than bad with AI, so it should stay open to everyone.

* He drew the line at catastrophic risks, like losing control of AI.

* He took a shot at Anthropic, calling the idea of one San Francisco lab controlling AI a completely unacceptable trade-off.

He still agreed with Dario Amodei's call last month to slow down the most advanced models.

The same weekend, the man in charge of OpenAI's safety reports for 12 major launches explained [in The Atlantic](https://www.theatlantic.com/technology/2026/10/openai-safety-team-resignation/688881/) why he quit.

He says OpenAI keeps sprinting from one launch to the next without the care AI needs, and that the time for trial and error is over. He wants AI labs run like nuclear plants.

As far as he knows, he never worked with anyone at OpenAI who'd kept airplanes or nuclear reactors safe.


----------







----------

80251.subject: AVALANCHE SEPTEMBER 2026 RECAP
80251.body:
View this post on the web at https://www.team1.blog/p/avalanche-september-2026-recap

Summit was the center of gravity for September, and everything else orbited it. Over two days in New York, Avalanche turned the stage into a live feed of institutional breaking news: Ethena’s Avalanche-exclusive neobank, South Korea committing its capital markets onchain, Hanwha’s tokenization platform, and UAE PASS serving 12 million people on national identity rails.
Asset managers from Janus Henderson to Goldman Sachs showed up with real allocations, Kevin O’Leary headlined, and the team closed it out calling it the most impactful Summit yet. Helicon also activated on mainnet during the same stretch, and Avalanche closed the month leading every chain in tokenized stock inflows and RWA growth.
Here’s everything that happened.
Want to keep up with the latest in the Avalanche ecosystem? Subscribe to the Team1 blog and get our updates in your inbox weekly.
September’s biggest technical story was Helicon going live, alongside record-setting weeks for tokenized assets.
Avalanche Turns Six:
The Avalanche genesis block was minted six years ago this month. [Genesis [ https://substack.com/redirect/4ce7c59e-f7d3-43c2-8f17-a2f712332a55?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ]]
Helicon Goes Live on Mainnet:
Helicon brought Continuous Execution for a faster C-Chain, auto-renewing staking, 48-hour minimum staking periods, and a new reward curve designed to reduce AVAX issuance. [Helicon [ https://substack.com/redirect/3e74af81-705d-47d8-9040-6af7f142c123?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ]]
Tokenized Assets Set New Records:
Avalanche pulled in $131.2 million in tokenized stock inflows over seven days, eight times the second-highest chain, while its RWA market cap grew $266 million over 30 days, more than the next two chains combined. [Stock Inflows [ https://substack.com/redirect/0b98c7be-764b-4055-8529-2ba66da0c1ab?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ]] | [RWA Growth [ https://substack.com/redirect/b745c30c-daf8-40ec-b38e-9891f23d3519?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ]]
Team1 Expands Across New Chapters and Continents:
Team1 opened new ground this month: the UK held its first event outside London in Chesterfield, while Amsterdam and Sofia each hosted their first Connect. Thailand officially launched as a chapter following a six-university workshop tour.
Elsewhere, Türkiye ran its first AI agent workshop, Ghana held its Blockchain and AI workshop, and a 50-builder residency took place in Bursa. Korea and Brazil held Builder Connects, while LatAm met with 20+ builders at Bolivia’s EthereumBo Buildathon. Team1 also hosted a rooftop meetup with The Grotto in NYC during Summit week, alongside many other events across different continents.
